- One branch/leaf is completely dead (brown-gray, dried/shriveled) hanging from the infected node
- The surrounding foliage remains green and healthy

**Comparison to reference images:**
- **Phytophthora_Blight (Bugwood_10)**: Strongest visual match — showed a very similar dark brown/black stem lesion at a node on the same type of plant, with similar discoloration pattern running along the stem

- **Gray_Mold**: Showed fruit mold and leaf necrosis, not a focal stem canker
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: White mycelial growth with sclerotia — clearly doesn't match
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt**: Shows vascular discoloration and fruit bird's-eye spots — doesn't match external dark stem appearance
- **Bacterial_Wilt/Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Basal discoloration and root rot — not matching
- All other classes (Early Blight, Septoria, Bacterial Speck, Mosaic viruses, etc.) showed leaf spots, mosaic patterns, or fruit symptoms — clearly different

The dark stem canker at a node causing death of the single branch above, while the rest of the plant stays green, best matches **Phytophthora Blight**.
